name: Refugios de la Guerra Civil, Almería (air-raid shelters)
story: Almería, the Republic's main port on the south-east coast, was bombed repeatedly from the air and the sea — the local memory association counts 57 raids. The worst single attack came at dawn on 31 May 1937, when the German cruiser Admiral Scheer and four destroyers shelled the city in reprisal for a Republican air attack on the cruiser Deutschland off Ibiza; around 19–20 civilians died. In response the city dug one of Europe's largest civilian shelter networks: more than 4 km of galleries about 9 m underground, built 1936–38 for some 40,000 people, with an operating theatre and store rooms. The city was also swollen by refugees from the fall of Málaga in February 1937.
see: About 1 km of restored galleries, the underground operating theatre, a food store and an introductory video; entrance kiosk on Plaza Manuel Pérez García.
plan: Temporarily closed for works. When open: guided visits only (in Spanish, c. 1 hour), tickets in advance at almeriaculturaentradas.es or by phone (950 268 696). Small fee.

boxes.text: Capacity and number of raids vary between sources (40,000 people is the usual figure; the memorial association says over 75% of the population). Deaths in the 31 May 1937 bombardment are given as 19–20.
